_leadership_summary:
The national 5-Star average advanced from 3.19 in January to 3.32 in July, a net gain of 0.13 points, with the portfolio peaking at 3.36 in June before a modest 0.04 pullback in the most recent period. This improvement was driven predominantly by Win Score, which climbed 0.25 points over the period from 2.80 to 3.05, and Hutbot Ontime, which gained 0.37 points from 3.54 to 3.91 — the strongest component-level advances in the dataset. Speed deteriorated modestly from 2.94 to 2.84, while Brand held flat at 3.33 and FSCC remained essentially plateaued near ceiling at 4.85. The tier migration story reflects meaningful upward mobility: 1,107 stores moved to a higher-performing tier versus 730 that declined, yielding a net positive migration of 377 stores. Tier 1 — the lowest-performing cohort — contracted by 186 stores from 1,014 to 828, an 18.3% reduction, while Tier 3 expanded by 219 stores from 850 to 1,069, a 25.8% increase. Tier 2 remained largely stable, shedding just 30 stores to settle at 2,755. Within tiers, scores were essentially flat: Tier 1 averaged 2.02 at start and 2.06 at close, Tier 2 moved from 3.26 to 3.30, and Tier 3 held at 4.37, indicating that the gains were driven by stores crossing tier thresholds rather than within-tier score compression.

Portfolio health remains a concern at the tail end. The 828 Tier 1 stores represent 17.7% of the system and remain the most operationally vulnerable cohort, with Win Score standing as the binding constraint at 63.7% — more than double the next-closest factor. Tier 2's 2,755 stores, comprising 58.8% of the portfolio, face a dual constraint of Win Score at 43.7% and Speed at 33.9%, suggesting that roughly one in three Tier 2 stores is operationally limited by delivery or carryout pace. Tier 3's 1,069 stores, while the strongest cohort, are not without friction: Speed at 35.7% is the primary limiter, followed by Win Score at 31.5% and Brand at 29.8%, pointing to an opportunity to accelerate top-tier performance through speed and brand-building initiatives. The risk exposure is material — 274 stores are currently defaulting, 29 are flagged at-risk, and 452 Tier 1 stores remain on watch — representing a combined 755 stores requiring active intervention. Correlations between 5-Star performance and same-store sales growth (0.10) and same-store transaction growth (0.11) remain positive but modest, underscoring that 5-Star gains translate to financial outcomes, though the relationship is not yet强driving.

Geographically, Danielle Hudson's zone delivered the strongest improvement at +0.32 points to a 3.39 average across 421 stores, anchored by a 76.9% increase in Tier 3 count and a 33.0% reduction in Tier 1 — the most dramatic tier migration of any zone. AKM Shaju posted the second-highest gain at +0.24 to 3.57 across 394 stores, with a 53.1% Tier 3 expansion and a 28.0% Tier 1 reduction. Dustin Patton leads all zones in average score at 3.72 with a +0.16 delta, supported by a 39.8% Tier 3 increase. Conversely, Kathleen Basbagill's zone trails at 2.90 average despite a +0.09 improvement, with 88 of her 274 stores — nearly a third — still in Tier 1. Sergio Villasenor and Sarah Heitz both sit at 3.06, though Villasenor's +0.18 delta suggests accelerating momentum. Among franchisees, AL SALAS (49 stores, 4.09 avg) and MARK PETERSON (68 stores, 4.05 avg) lead the system, both operating above the Tier 3 threshold across their portfolios. At the other end, ASAD ADAM MITHA (7 stores, 1.70 avg), JAKE RASOR (1 store, 1.85 avg), and KETANKUMAR PATEL (29 stores, 1.87 avg) represent the most distressed operators, all falling well below Tier 1 entry and requiring immediate coaching intervention.

The primary national priority must be Win Score acceleration, particularly for the 828 Tier 1 stores where it accounts for 63.7% of binding constraint share — without meaningful Win Score improvement, these stores cannot migrate to Tier 2 regardless of performance on other components. For the 2,755-store Tier 2 middle, a dual focus on Win Score and Speed is essential to unlocking Tier 3 entry at scale. Operational recommendations include: deploying targeted Speed playbooks to zones where it is the binding constraint (Hudson, Shaju, and Lobaccaro zones), accelerating brand-building activities in Tier 3 to capture the 29.8% Brand constraint opportunity, and intensifying coaching cadence on the 274 defaulting stores and 452 Tier 1 watch stores to stem further risk. The 0.10 correlation between 5-Star and SSSG validates that these operational improvements carry direct financial upside, and the net positive tier migration of 377 stores demonstrates the system is moving in the right direction — but the pace of Tier 1 reduction must accelerate to meaningfully de-risk the portfolio.
